episodes.191353: A burst of record level monsoonal moisture flowed into NM coupled with a backdoor frontal boundary moving through eastern NM. This yielded scattered to numerous afternoon thunderstorms developing over the high terrain of central and western NM on June 29th. One batch developed directly over the new South Fork burn scar along the Lincoln and Otero County line just west of Ruidoso. This storm expanded in coverage eastward toward Alto and Ruidoso, producing burn scar flash flooding and debris flows throughout the area. Nearly all if not all drainages into the Rio Ruidoso exhibited thick debris flows through town, warranting an evacuation of the Upper Canyon area. Numerous streets and water crossings were inundated with debris flows and flash flooding. Emergency officials reported there being 26 swift water rescues in Ruidoso on June 29th with zero injuries or fatalities. Heavy rains spread into the Rio Grande Valley and East Mountain Communities that evening. The torrential downpours produced 1 to 2 inches of rainfall over the ABQ metro in as little as one hour resulting in flash flooding across town. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities thankfully. Heavy rains returned to the Ruidoso area on June 30th in the form of storms anchored over the high terrain. Rainfall totals were estimated to be as high as 4 to 6 inches over portions of the Salt burn scar located just south of the Otero County line. Flash flooding and debris flows drained northward into Ruidoso and Ruidoso Downs to Hollywood. Another flash flood emergency was issued as a result and the torrential debris flows raged through U.S. Highway 70 with the worst of it focused near the Sudderth Drive intersection. Multiple vehicles were swept away, including a semi-truck. A sharp rise on the Rio Ruidoso was recorded reaching Minor flood stage again, just as it did on the 29th. Damage to businesses and the Ruidoso Hospital were reported.
episodes.191361: A cold front moved across a moderately unstable airmass across Vermont during the afternoon. Scattered thunderstorms developed in central VT and intensified as they moved east into NH. One thunderstorm caused minor wind damage in two communities in Orange county.
episodes.191403: Flooding occurred along the Salmon River Road as brief but intense rainfall occurred.
episodes.191418: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front in a hot and moist airmass. Storms produced heavy rain and flooding in poor drainage areas.
episodes.191431: A thunderstorm tracked across the northwest part of the Denver Metro area producing hail up to one inch in diameter.
episodes.191438: A cold front began moving across central Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening hours of June 30, 2024 with severe thunderstorms forming ahead of and along the frontal boundary. This frontal boundary, with ample moisture and instability produced sporadic thunderstorm wind damage and small hail in the Lower Susquehanna Valley and in portions of the Middle Susquehanna Valley.
episodes.191444: A line of thunderstorms produced localized wind damage over northern Maryland.
episodes.191445: Several bands and clusters of thunderstorms produced scattered instances of wind damage mainly near and east of Interstate 95 in Maryland and northern Virginia. There were a few instances of considerable wind damage in Maryland.
episodes.191446: Several bands and clusters of thunderstorms produced scattered instances of wind damage mainly near and east of Interstate 95 in Maryland and northern Virginia. There were a few instances of considerable wind damage in Maryland.
episodes.191449: Multiple bands and clusters of thunderstorms produced strong winds over area waterways during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.191532: A pre-frontal surface trough led to the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms across the eastern Piedmont and Coastal Plain of central North Carolina in the afternoon and early evening hours. These storms led to some isolated reports of trees down in Granville County.
episodes.191539: Numerous strong to severe thunderstorms formed primarily in Santa Cruz and Cochise Counties during the afternoon of June 30. A couple of locations such as St. David and Patagonia experienced severe criteria winds.
episodes.191596: Heavy rain fell across portions of Robertson and Sumner counties during the early morning hours of June 30, 2024. Official measurements showed 3 to 3.5 inches of rain in a short period of time, and the White House area was hardest hit by flooding with numerous homes reported flooded.
episodes.191608: A round of thunderstorms brought a few damaging winds to Rhode Island.
episodes.191609: A round of thunderstorms brought wind damage and flash flooding to Connecticut.
episodes.191622: On the afternoon of June 29th, strong to severe thunderstorms quickly developed during peak heating hours with the help of a nearby cold front and unseasonably hot temperatures across northeast Kentucky. Strong wind gusts accompanying these storms caused several areas of downed trees and power lines in Greenup and Boyd Counties. There was also an instance of flash flooding in downtown Ashland, where a passing storm produced heavy downpours that flooded a local road during the afternoon and into the evening of the 29th. Storms quickly progressed into West Virginia that evening, bringing the risk of severe weather to an end that day.
episodes.191634: Long hodographs and deep inverted-V soundings resulted in organized convection across Southwest Montana June 30. Hail was the main severe observation, but a wind gust of 58 mph was also observed.
episodes.191933: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms impacted portions of southeast Wyoming from the mid afternoon through the early evening hours on 6/30, producing several instances of large hail in excess of one inch in diameter as well as wind gusts between 60 and 70 MPH. Most notably, a cluster of intense thunderstorms tracked across central Laramie County roughly between 7 PM and 9 PM MDT, producing 70 to 80 MPH wind gusts and reportedly damaging several outbuildings in the northern outskirts of Cheyenne.
episodes.192007: During a concert following the Mud Bash at the Milan Dragway, a single lightning strike struck 4 individuals, who reported tingling sensations. Two of these individuals were transported to the hospital for further treatment and released.
episodes.192067: A cold front sweeping across the region produced a mesoscale convective system ahead of it, this MCS produced a couple isolated reports of damaging wind gusts.
episodes.192068: A cold front sweeping across the region produced a mesoscale convective system ahead of it, this MCS produced a couple isolated reports of damaging wind gusts.
episodes.192113: Scattered thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a cold front, and were most numerous over the Catskills and Sullivan County. A few storms became severe, producing damaging wind gusts that mainly knocked down trees and wires. However, one storm produced a severe microburst that cause damage at two separate campgrounds in Delaware County, with one injury and one fatality when a tree fell through a camper.
episodes.192114: Scattered thunderstorms developed over Northeastern Pennsylvania ahead of an approaching cold front. A few storms became severe producing damaging wind gusts that mainly knocked down trees and wires.
episodes.192536: A cold front tracking south east across eastern New York brought scattered showers and thunderstorms, some of which became severe in the Mid-Hudson Valley and Eastern Catskills. Severe thunderstorms resulted in numerous reports of downed trees and wires, some of which resulted in structural damage to a house and apartment building, in addition to nearly 5000 people without power.
episodes.192537: A cold front tracking south east across northwest Connecticut brought scattered showers and thunderstorms, some of which became severe in Litchfield County. Severe thunderstorms resulted in numerous reports of downed trees and wires, in addition to nearly 500 people without power. Additionally, heavy rain resulted in an isolated instance of flash flooding wherein Route 199 in Roxbury was washed out in the town of Washington.
episodes.192548: Afternoon thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce a waterspout over Estero Bay near Bonita Springs in Lee County. The waterspout very briefly became a tornado as it crossed over a 200-foot diameter swath of an uninhabited island in the bay before again becoming a waterspout after crossing the island.
episodes.192549: Afternoon thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce a waterspout over Estero Bay near Bonita Springs in Lee County. The waterspout very briefly became a tornado as it crossed over a 200-foot diameter swath of an uninhabited island in the bay before again becoming a waterspout after crossing the island.
episodes.192609: Scattered thunderstorms developed near a surface front across northern Oklahoma during the early evening of the 29th. Sufficient deep-layer wind shear and instability promoted an environment capable of transiently organized thunderstorms. A few such storms developed across north-central Oklahoma, producing reports of large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.192632: A mid-level trough and surface pre-frontal trough and cold front approached the area. Thunderstorms fired up along the pre-frontal trough and moved towards the area. The storms formed a line and moved into southern CT, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.192633: A mid-level trough and surface pre-frontal trough and cold front approached the area. Thunderstorms fired up along the pre-frontal trough and moved towards the area. The storms formed a line and moved into northeastern NJ, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.192634: A mid-level trough and surface pre-frontal trough and cold front approached the area. Thunderstorms fired up along the pre-frontal trough and moved towards the area. The storms formed a line and moved into southeastern NY, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.192635: A mid-level trough and surface pre-frontal trough and cold front approached the area. Thunderstorms fired up along the pre-frontal trough and moved towards the area. The storms formed a line and moved over the waters, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.192686: Low pressure tracking north of Maine drew a cold front across the region during the afternoon of the 30th. Thunderstorms developed in advance of the front. Some of the thunderstorms reached severe levels producing damaging winds. A downburst in the vicinity of Brownville Junction...Piscataquis county...produced wind gusts estimated at up to 70 mph. In excess of 50 trees were toppled or snapped along with power lines and utility poles leading to power outages.
episodes.192859: Strong thunderstorms produced a 35 knot wind gust at the Panama City Marina.
episodes.192904: Strong thunderstorms were able to thrive on the afternoon of June 29th across southeast Ohio in response to an approaching cold front and unseasonably hot temperatures festering over the area. Storms that developed in Ohio progressed through Lawrence County and inflicted strong enough wind gusts to promote downed trees and power lines through local communities. Severe weather was brief on this day for southeast Ohio, as storms then traveled east of the Ohio River and into West Virginia.
episodes.192971: In the midst of abnormally hot conditions around the region, strong to severe thunderstorms thrived across West Virginia on June 29th and 30th. On both days, storms initially developed during peak heating hours and progressed through the state before diminishing with the loss of daytime heating. Storm damage was mainly observed in the form of downed trees each day.
episodes.192979: Slow moving thunderstorms produced localized flash flooding across the area.
episodes.193005: In addition to a mid-level disturbance, deep tropical moisture continued to filter into the southern Florida Peninsula on June 30. With plentiful instability and around peak diurnal heating led to showers and thunderstorms across southwestern Florida. With light steering flow, storm motions were slow, which when combined with heavy downpours, resulted in localized flooding across portions of western Collier County.
episodes.193006: A mid-level disturbance moved across the southern peninsula of Florida on June 30th, which led to abundant convective activity across the region. Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across the eastern metropolitan area, especially Broward County, throughout the morning and early afternoon.
episodes.193014: Weak steering flow over a saturated airmass where precipitable water over 2.3 inches combined with sea breeze forcing created high rainfall rates and slow-moving storms.
episodes.193023: On June 30, a cluster of storms, along a cold front, dropped to the southeast through central Kentucky. The storms brought down trees which also brought down power lines in Nelson and Marion Counties.
episodes.193034: A brief funnel cloud was reported near Belzoni. No damage was reported.
episodes.193106: A slow moving cold front allowed for widespread thunderstorm development on June 30th. MUCAPE values of 2000-3000 J/kg with PWATs near 2 allowed for thunderstorms to produce heavy rainfall with rainfall rates of 1-2 inches per hour. These thunderstorms moved through the Lower Hudson Valley and Connecticut resulting in 1 to 2 inches of rain, most of which fell over a one to two hour period. This resulted in localized flash flooding.
episodes.193107: A slow moving cold front allowed for widespread thunderstorm development on June 30th. MUCAPE values of 2000-3000 J/kg with PWATs near 2 allowed for thunderstorms to produce heavy rainfall with rainfall rates of 1-2 inches per hour. These thunderstorms moved through the Lower Hudson Valley and Connecticut resulting in 1 to 2 inches of rain, most of which fell over a one to two hour period. This resulted in localized flash flooding.
episodes.193130: While a cold front was slowly approaching the state from the NW on the day of June 29, a secondary boundary set up to the southeast, spanning across southcentral to northeast Kentucky. Along this boundary storms began to fire in the afternoon, creating a broken line. While most of the storms were strong but not severe, one storm in particular out-performed the rest in eastern Kentucky, resulting in both a Severe Thunderstorm Warning and Flash Flood Warning for Bath, Fleming, and Rowan counties in the northern portion of the JKL CWA. Fleming County dispatch received reports of several downed trees as the storm rolled through, all concentrated near the town of Tilton.
episodes.193135: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across southeastern Kansas during the early evening of the 29th, as a cold front moved into the area. The thunderstorms developed south during the evening, and produced damaging wind gusts as they moved through northeastern Oklahoma.
episodes.193139: A cold front moved into southwest Virginia early on June 30th, proceeding to stall out near the Blue Ridge mountains. The front interacted with a unstable, highly saturated environment to create scattered thunderstorms in southwest Virginia. Some of these storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.193155: An upper level disturbance approached New England from the west during the afternoon hours of the 30th.  A surface cold front associated with the upper level wave interacted with hot and unstable conditions to allow for numerous thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon hours.  Some of the storms became severe with damaging winds and a few reports of large hail impacted mostly the Central and Southern parts of the state.
episodes.193156: An upper level disturbance approached New England from the west during the afternoon hours of the 30th. A surface cold front associated with the upper level wave interacted with hot and unstable conditions to allow for numerous thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon hours. Some of the storms became severe with damaging winds and a few reports of large hail impacted mostly the Western half of the state.
episodes.193170: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed out ahead of and along a cold front crossing the area. Severe thunderstorms were confined to eastern portions of the forecast area, from Wayne and Ontario counties eastward.
episodes.193230: An upper high was located over northeast Texas with modest low and mid level moisture brought into the Borderland on southeast winds.  Dew point depressions over the lowlands were still around 50 degrees supporting strong downburst winds with the strongest thunderstorms that developed.
episodes.193231: Deeper monsoonal moisture moved into the region with a strong upper high located across northeast Texas.  Deep southeast winds brought the best moisture of the year into the Borderland which produced strong thunderstorm wind gusts in Dona Ana and Sierra counties along with a gustnado near Chaparral.
episodes.193362: Well above average rainfall throughout June in conjunction with late-month heavy rainfall contributed to additional rises into flood stage along the Mississippi River. River gauges at both Guttenberg and Lansing reached minor flood stage before the end of the month and observed rising river levels into July.
episodes.193378: Monsoon moisture brougth strong to severe thunderstorms to parts of northern Arizona.
episodes.193407: A thunderstorm became severe over southwest portions of Weston County and tracked northeast across the county before weakening as it moved into South Dakota. The storm produced wind gusts to 70 mph from the Rochelle area to near Newcastle.
episodes.193675: A thunderstorm brought strong wind to northern Natrona County. Wind gusts of 59 mph were reported along Interstate 25 to the west of Midwest.
episodes.193744: An upper level disturbance drifted southwestward over the Florida Keys, aiding in the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms over the Lower Florida Keys.
episodes.193808: A very warm and moist airmass was in place as a strong cold front moved into the Mid-Atlantic. This resulted in several showers and thunderstorms developing, which brought damaging wind gusts, knocking down trees and power lines across portions of eastern Pennsylvania.
episodes.193809: A very warm and moist airmass was in place as a strong cold front moved into the Mid-Atlantic. This resulted in several showers and thunderstorms developing, which brought damaging wind gusts, knocking down trees and power lines across portions of New Jersey.
episodes.193873: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of central, south central and southeast Virginia.
episodes.193874: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.193875: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of central and southeast Virginia.
episodes.193880: A low pressure moving into the Great Basin with high pressure to the east allowed deeper sub-tropical moisture to increase across the area. The best moisture remained across southeast Utah and southwest Colorado with a later start to storm development due to morning cloud cover. Heavy rain occurred with some storms with minor street flooding occurring in Mesa County and Garfield County.
episodes.193886: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.193887: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the York River.
episodes.193909: An embedded wave was transitioning over the region, resulting in the development of stronger storms, which produced heavy rain. Thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall resulted in flooded roadways in some areas in Pueblo, CO.
episodes.193928: Scattered thunderstorms developed over upstate South Carolina during the afternoon. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.193929: Scattered thunderstorms developed over western North Carolina during the afternoon. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.194013: Scattered severe thunderstorms tracked across south central and southeast Kansas beginning during the afternoon hours of the 29th and lasting into the late evening hours. These storms produced quarter to baseball sized hail and damaging wind gusts up to 75 mph; damage occurred to trees and power poles. There was one landspout reported inear Yates Center. Heavy rain persisted over south central Kansas which led to flash flooding in Kingman.

Heavy rain measured to have ranged from 1 to 2 inches within one hour across the Albuquerque metro area caused major flash flooding. Underpasses and low lying intersections in downtown were inundated with deep floodwaters. An SUV and public transit bus were partially submerged under the water and had to be retrieved by a tow truck. There were reports of street flooding and vehicles being stranded elsewhere across town. The Albuquerque Fire Department reported they performed 7 swift water rescues in the arroyos around town and 18 overall responses to folks impacted by the floodwaters. Of these responses, 10 were to help people stranded. An unknown number of homes near downtown and south of downtown received flood damage. The Albuquerque Police Department, Convention Center and City Hall also experienced flooding, but the damage was mostly aesthetic according to media reports. Total damage is an estimate based on limited information and extent of damage.

A severe microburst with estimated wind speeds of up to 90 mph, occurred just northwest to north of Cooks Falls, NY near the southeastern edge of Delaware County. There was sporadic damage spread across southern Delaware County from the severe thunderstorm that tracked through the area late in the morning. However, straight-line wind damage was most concentrated in a microburst footprint that encompassed Cooks Hollow and Butternut Grove in the Beaver Kill Valley, and especially up the Russell Brook drainage for at least a mile. The damage pattern diverged from the middle of the path, indicative of a downburst.||This severe microburst impacted two campgrounds with very damaging straight line winds. Many recreational vehicles and camper units, a few tents, and at least two vehicles were heavily damaged and in some cases destroyed by falling trees. Some of the trees or large branches exceeded a foot in diameter. A woman unfortunately perished when a large tree snapped and fell on her site, crushing it. At least one other person was injured with a hit to the head. There was an unknown number of additional |though minor injuries. Eyewitnesses reported that the winds came up suddenly and then lasted at least 5 minutes with one tree after another falling during that period.

A line of thunderstorms produced a downburst...almost a mile in length...in the vicinity of Brownville Junction producing straight line wind gusts estimated at up to 70 mph. Numerous trees  were toppled or snapped along with utility poles and downed wires. Extensive power outages occurred in the vicinity of the downburst. Along Front Street in Brownville Junction approximately 10 medium to large pine trees were snapped. Several trees were toppled along Davis Street in Brownville. Approximately 20 to 30 trees were uprooted...approximately 10 snapped in a wooded lot along Route 11. An RV park along Route 11 also received damage. Several campers received damage to awnings...with several tents also damaged. Several large pieces of decor...including a canoe...were blown to the ground at the entrance to the park.  Further north along Route 11...large individual trees were snapped or toppled on to power lines at several locations. Route 11 was shut down between Brownville and Millinocket due to fallen trees and power lines blocking the road.

Two outflows from nearby thunderstorms collided over the Chaparral area which created a gustnado as well as straight-line wind damage. There was a complete collapse of a well built outbuilding/garage.  The roof separated from the walls allowing the wind to get inside and under the roof structure.  The roof debris scattered towards the west and northwest and was displaced approximately 50 yards from the foundation. The walls collapsed afterwards with all of the walls falling in a southward direction.  Metal fencing attached to a rock wall was ripped off.  An RV camper rolled on it's side and was damaged by flying debris. There was a metal shed that collapsed as winds lifted the roof from the structure.  Finally, an outdoor shed was completely destroyed with debris scattered up to 100 yards towards the northwest.

Slow moving storms developed over the burn scars near Ruidoso with an estimated 4 to 6 inches of rainfall on the eastern half of the Salt burn scar. Flash flooding and debris flow raged down drainages along U.S. Highway 70 to the Ruidoso Hospital and intersection with Sudderth Road. The NM National Guard reported conducting 45 swift water rescues through the day and early evening, including an unknown number at the Rainbow Lake RV Park on Carrizozo Canyon Road. Roads were also impassable at Brady Canyon Rd., Porr Dr., Leon Farrar Dr., University Dr. and Mechem Dr., among others. Video was captured of the torrent of flood waters and debris flow sweeping a dumpster and multiple vehicles down U.S. Highway 70, including a semi-truck. An evacuation was ordered for the Upper Canyon area of Ruidoso. Miraculously, there were no reports of injury or fatalities. Damage is an estimate.

Flash flooding and mudslides occurred along Salmon River Road from just above Ebenezer Campground to just below Owl Creek. Radar estimates of up to 1.25 inches of rain fell over a half hour period across the southern half of the Owl Creek Basin. There were three major slides along the Salmon River Road, near Poverty Flat, Skull Gulch, and one roughly 0.3 miles in length where the road bank collapsed into the river. The Skull Gulch slide destroyed at least one outbuilding. There were also 30 to 50 additional small slides across the Salmon River Road that didn't cause structural damage.
